summary: Truncate partitions lose rows near the minimum int or long. Equality, in and range filters miss them, because the writer wraps the partition value and the scan does not. Fix PR apache/iceberg-python#4407 is open.
Scans on year and month partitions raised OverflowError at 9999-12-31 and 0001-01-01, and filters on inf in a float column returned wrong rows. apache/iceberg-python#4406 fixed it.

The Kafka source drops offsets for partitions with no messages since the last start. With the default settings, two quiet restarts lose every message written while the pipeline was stopped. Idle partitions replay and duplicate.

Concurrent UPDATE, upsert and transfer writes that reported success were silently lost on 1.5.1. We added that evidence to this existing issue. dolthub/doltgresql#3887 fixed it: such commits now fail with a serialization error.
NOT EXISTS over a nullable foreign key panicked in the merge join. dolthub/doltgresql#3911 fixed it. Indexes matched PostgreSQL across 150 queries on 11 index variants.

Most statements DuckDB ran matched PostgreSQL 17. Three differences ordinary queries hit: division by zero returns Infinity instead of an error, a LIKE pattern that is a function call fails (Django's icontains), and round(float8) rounds halves away from zero.

SUM over a DECIMAL column stops the pipeline when identical rows in one batch make value times weight overflow 38 digits, even though the true sum fits. The maintainers confirmed that an overflow is meant to stop the pipeline, so this is designed behavior, not a bug.

ROLLUP, CUBE and GROUPING SETS views returned no rows on an empty table, where PostgreSQL and DuckDB return the grand-total row. The row also disappeared after the last row was deleted. feldera/feldera#8034 fixed it.

The open-source edition, 0.383.0, held up against its own docs: views matched a recompute under churn, at 1, 4 and 8 workers, and for every SQL type. The maintainers asked us to file its two edge cases. One was a bug, now fixed (#8033). The other is designed behavior (#8032).
AsyncFileSystemWrapper silently discarded writes: open, touch and async_wrapper:: URLs lost the data. fsspec/filesystem_spec#2473 fixed it.
pipe_file(mode="create") overwrites an existing file on simplecache and on the reference filesystem. Fix PRs #2482 and #2486 are open.
ReferenceFileSystem.find returns sibling keys, such as x_bnds/0 for x, and ignores maxdepth.
ArrowFSWrapper.rm rejects a list of paths, so FSMap.delitems raises TypeError on Arrow. Fix PR #2481 is open.
Redis storage breaks the Storage contract: Iterator returns no keys at 5,000 keys, and IteratorWithRange and Seek ignore their arguments. Memory IteratorWithRange includes its limit.
Makes Memory IteratorWithRange exclude its limit. Adds a regression test.
Temper contract tests across the storage backends.

On pandas[pyarrow], to_dict turns ints into floats and nulls into NaN. On DuckDB and SQLFrame, a select of only literals returns one row per input row. A fix PR for to_dict, narwhals-dev/narwhals#4167, is open.
Three columns read correctly from memory but break after compaction to Parquet: nullable bool reads back false, int32 makes queries fail, repeated uint64 makes compaction fail.
Fixes the three compaction bugs with a regression test.
Adds Temper and the Arrow type lattice that found the bugs.

executemany in autocommit commits nothing on libpq 14+ but commits the rows before a failure on libpq 13. Prepared statements go stale after a repeated DROP or DISCARD ALL. The C loaders wrap very large intervals. Three smaller type bugs. The maintainer closed it.
Rolling and cumulative argmin/argmax return negative indices at the array edges on main, a regression from #11696. Fixed by pydata/xarray#11900.
With numbagg installed, flox's default path makes groupby any treat NaN as False. use_flox=False and NumPy treat NaN as true.
Under flox, groupby sum and prod apply min_count to integers and return float64 with NaN. The docstring and use_flox=False ignore min_count for integers.
With use_bottleneck=True, rolling argmin and argmax pick the last tied value, while NumPy picks the first.

Writes that FLUSH acknowledged as durable are lost when the meta node crashes: 10 of 10 runs on v3.1.2 and 9 of 10 on main lost acknowledged inserts, and a single crash was enough in 5 of 10. dml_wait_persistence lost nothing.

Strong consistency held: views matched their batch queries in every snapshot under concurrent writes, and compute, frontend and compactor crashes lost no acknowledged write. Two subscription gaps: early changes are lost, and the documented resume recipe re-delivers rows.

Go, JS, Ruby and Rust held River's documented guarantees under worker and Postgres faults, with all five clients in one database. Three findings: a cancel lost during a rescue (Go), Java's complete(connection) committing an effect twice, and periodic uniqueness keyed on insert time (Go and Java).
SQL Pub/Subs deliver duplicates across a database restart despite ExactlyOnceDelivery. MySQL Publish blocks while a message is unacked. The HTTP Pub/Sub never runs the shared test suite.
Fixes the TestReconnect retry log, which printed a nil error.
Adds an opt-in reconnect-tests input to the shared CI workflow.
The Temper matrix for the SQL Pub/Subs, for reference.
Turns on Kafka's reconnect tests.
Runs Temper beside the SQLFlow coverage gate. The first matrix shows 164 covered and 0 failing cells. Temper found two exemptions whose proving tests did not exist, and the PR adds those tests.

nchunks_initialized and info_complete() raise when a sibling array's name starts with the array's name (lat, lat_bnds), because stores disagree on list_prefix. Byte-range edge cases differ across stores. Fix PR zarr-developers/zarr-python#4653 is open.
